Isolate the production database and autoscale ingress without changing the app release (#1765)

Production currently shares two nodes between the registry database,
application and ingress. Enable one dedicated database node plus 2–3
worker nodes, reserve the DB's existing three-CPU quota, and scale
ingress from 3–6 replicas. This is an explicitly authorized production
experiment; staging has not passed full burst/recovery acceptance.

Keep registry 1.8.6 and two fixed app replicas. That binary hardcodes 60
connections per replica, so staging's 3–4 app HPA and 30/5 pool
configuration cannot be promoted as an infrastructure-only change. App
CPU requests become 800m; networking and the DB volume remain unchanged.

Add a manual read-only production preview and refresh state before
apply. Keep staging behavior unchanged and derive the database pool name
from the stack's project. The singleton DB move may briefly interrupt
requests; monitor the transition and the next real traffic cycle.

Validation: deployment Go tests passed; deployment binary built; diff
checks passed. CI and production preview must pass before merge.

Prepare listing JSON and stage isolated database capacity (#1756)

Cyclic listing bursts hold database connections while application
decoding competes with ingress and PostgreSQL for CPU. This change
closes listing rows before typed decoding, prepares versioned listing
JSON during writes, and adds checkout timing, opt-in loopback profiling
and configurable per-replica pools. Derived JSON preserves metadata,
invalidates on old-writer updates, falls back for unknown codecs and has
a bounded backfill tool.

**Production acceptance is still pending. The new placement is running
in staging; production has not changed.**

### Staging capacity and placement

The staging-only profile uses one fixed, tainted e2-standard-4 database
node and two–three e2-standard-4 workers: three total idle nodes, four
under load. PostgreSQL requests its full 3-CPU limit. App and ingress
require worker nodes and retain per-revision hostname spread. Apps scale
3–4 with 800m requests and pools 30/5; ingress scales 3–6 with 800m CPU
/ 512Mi memory requests. Both CPU targets are 70%, with conservative
scale-down. The prepared-listing staging image is digest-pinned.
Production enablement of this experimental profile is rejected.

PostgreSQL, three apps and three ingress replicas rolled out
successfully. All 48 saved response fixtures matched; the corpus
remained 52,366 names / 187,108 versions with zero invalid indexes. One
of 84 external health probes failed during rollout, so this was not an
interruption-free transition.

At 13:12:29 UTC on October 29, staging naturally consolidated to **one
DB node and two workers**, with all apps and ingress Ready: 2 apps + 1
ingress on one worker, 1 app + 2 ingress on the other. All 20 health
probes during idle observation succeeded. No forced eviction or resize
was used. This proves idle placement/consolidation, not loaded burst
recovery. System agents still share the DB node; PostgreSQL remains a
singleton. Node-upgrade surge can temporarily exceed four nodes. Public
networking was not changed.

### Staging deployment transition

The database pool and app HPA already exist from the staging experiment.
Before the normal staging apply, GitHub Actions will use its existing
staging passphrase secret to import these exact resources into Pulumi.
The adoption script skips completed imports, checks
stack/provider/resource identities and rejects conflicting ownership.
The DB pool is protected from deletion. Staging apply refreshes state
before planning.

Local adoption was blocked by the unavailable stack passphrase. The
script's plan was checked against the exported staging state, but **the
CI import/apply has not yet executed**. The pinned staging image
deliberately preserves the tested candidate until acceptance; remove
that override when returning to normal staging builds.

### Existing performance evidence and limits

The same ordered 274,116-read production trace was compared across
baseline, app only, and the earlier shared-node infrastructure
candidate. App-only sampled CPU fell approximately 31% (2.13 to 1.47
cores). Generator drops fell from 2.10% to 0.84%; attempted page p95
fell from 3,322 to 1,597 ms. The older infrastructure arm dropped 0.70%
and had seven transport failures. **All arms failed the short delivery
gate.**

Drops were confined to the initial 84 seconds of an abrupt replay into
empty ingress caches. Twelve final-minute
cache/body-size/key-diversity/query-mix checks passed, but this does not
qualify the startup cache state or full production cycle. Detail 404s
from the older staging corpus and single-source rate-limit 429s must be
resolved in the next comparison.

Earlier recovery completed 180,000/180,000 reads, but that was a
different two-replica/shared-node candidate. Its result is not credited
to this placement. The ten-minute peak and publish workload have not yet
been tested with the new layout.

### Validation and promotion gate

- Deployment-module Go tests and changed deployment-code lint passed.
- Five adoption tests passed, covering retries and rejection of wrong
stack, identity, provider or duplicate ownership;
workflows/configuration parsed as YAML.
- Existing application, benchmark, race and workload-fidelity validation
is retained in the linked reports.
- Before production promotion: replay preceding observed traffic to
establish cache state, then the selected peak with publish traffic and
recovery. Count all offered work, including generator drops; verify
per-replica sharing, CPU pressure, connection waits, errors/latency and
natural return to three nodes. Keep cold-cache startup as a separate
resilience test.

See [isolated placement and
evidence](https://github.com/modelcontextprotocol/registry/blob/codex/ingress-autoscaling/tools/ingressbench/ISOLATED_PLACEMENT.md),
[production trace
comparison](https://github.com/modelcontextprotocol/registry/blob/codex/ingress-autoscaling/tools/ingressbench/WORKLOAD_COMPARISON.md),
[workload
audit](https://github.com/modelcontextprotocol/registry/blob/codex/ingress-autoscaling/tools/ingressbench/WORKLOAD_PROFILE.md)
and [capacity
candidate](https://github.com/modelcontextprotocol/registry/blob/codex/ingress-autoscaling/tools/ingressbench/COORDINATED_CAPACITY.md).
